about:
Goodtime Medical operates from Wright City, Missouri, just outside St. Louis. The company has been manufacturing and selling medical furniture directly to customers for over three decades, though a precise founding year is not publicly disclosed. Ownership details and founder names have not been shared.

The company produces a broad line of commercial‑grade medical furniture, including exam tables (family, pediatric, and police‑car models), medical scales (infant, pediatric, and family), ADA‑compliant cabinets (wall, floating, kitchen, and bathroom vanities with porcelain or stainless‑steel tops), medical supply carts, medical stools, phlebotomy chairs, and adult and pediatric hospital beds. All items are manufactured in‑house and sold direct; the company cites a standard lead time of two to three weeks with rush‑order availability. Facility size, headcount, and annual volume are not disclosed.

Customers span medical and healthcare settings such as hospitals, clinics, pediatric practices, family‑practice offices, phlebotomy centers, and law‑enforcement agencies (evidenced by a police‑car pediatric exam table). Concrete product examples include the Elite Exam Table, Jungle Infant Scale, ADA Vanity 54, and Pro Series 600 Exam Table.

Goodtime Medical emphasizes its direct‑manufacturing model to eliminate middleman markups, offers a published 5 % discount code (4GTWNG46), and highlights a two‑to‑three‑week lead time with rush‑order flexibility as key differentiators.

name: Grace Technologies
old_description: Our GracePort and Grace Permanent Electrical Safety Devices (PESDs) drive innovation, enhance productivity and keep people safe and assets secure through simple and affordable solutions. Our GraceSense Predictive Maintenance System offers predictive maintenance capabilities and provide continuous monitoring and alert personnel when an unplanned shutdown is about to occur.
about:
Grace Technologies is headquartered in Davenport, Iowa. The company traces its roots to 1993 when founder Phil Allen, then a startup system integrator called Grace Engineering, encountered a hazardous electrical safety issue during a friction welder retrofit at John Deere. The solution he devised—a panel interface connector branded GracePort—launched the business, which later became Grace Engineered Products and, in 2020, Grace Technologies.

Today Grace manufactures three core product lines: GracePort panel interface connectors that provide thru-door access to PLCs and control panels; GracePESDs, permanent electrical safety devices that combine presence-of-voltage LED indication with absence-of-voltage test points for lockout/tagout; and the GraceSense predictive maintenance system, a line of IIoT smart sensors that continuously monitor vibration and temperature on switchgear, transformers, and rotating equipment. The catalog encompasses roughly 16,000 SKUs, and the company ships orders worldwide within two to three business days through a distribution network spanning more than 60 countries.

Customers include power plants, food and beverage facilities, chiller plants, and any operation that relies on evaporative cooling towers, as well as broader industrial facilities seeking to reduce incident energy exposure and unplanned downtime. The company’s predictive maintenance webinar series, co-hosted with Infinite Cooling, targets managers of those specific asset types.

Grace says its differentiation rests on four pillars: thought leadership from a team of forward‑thinking engineers; mass customization enabled by its deep SKU count; fast delivery via the 2‑3‑day global shipping promise; and a founding principle of being easy to do business with. Its stated mission is to pursue practical ways of keeping live voltage away from workers before, during, and after maintenance tasks, while empowering maintenance programs with IIoT sensor data.

name: Grado Creations
old_description: Grado Creations is a premier custom furniture and cabinetry manufacturer based in Albuquerque, New Mexico. Since 1998, we have specialized in crafting authentic, handmade Southwest-style furniture, bespoke kitchen cabinets, and one-of-a-kind wood pieces. Led by master craftsman Jose Grado, our workshop combines traditional hand-carving techniques with personalized design to deliver exceptional, durable woodwork to homes and retailers across the United States.
about:
Grado Creations is based in Albuquerque, New Mexico, and traces its origins to 1998 when master craftsman Jose Grado began building custom furniture and cabinetry with a Southwest aesthetic. The workshop initially focused on hand-carved wood pieces, bespoke kitchen cabinets, and one-of-a-kind furniture for homes and retailers across the United States.

Today the company has pivoted entirely to premium made-to-order home textiles. Its product line includes all-season quilted bedding sets, reversible water-resistant sofa slipcovers, absorbent area rugs and floor mats, and seasonal accents such as quilted tree skirts and laundry organizers. Production uses advanced direct-to-textile dye technology on high-density microfiber and poly-cotton blends, with multi-layer quilting, hypoallergenic batting, and reinforced perimeter stitching. Every item is printed, cut, and sewn individually after an order is placed, avoiding warehouse overstock.

The brand serves the home decor and lifestyle market, targeting consumers who want rustic, Southwestern-inspired textiles that withstand daily use by pets and children. Its direct-to-consumer channel ships nationwide, and the product assortment — exemplified by pet-proof sofa covers, machine-washable quilts, and cabin-themed bedding — is designed for practical, lived-in spaces.

Grado Creations says its differentiation lies in four pillars: authentic heritage-inspired designs rooted in Southwestern and lodge aesthetics; engineering for real-life durability (water-resistant, non-slip, machine-washable); a conscious made-to-order model that reduces textile waste; and transparent, US-based customer support with free shipping on orders over $150 and a 30-day return window.

name: Grand Central Wiring
old_description: Our mission is to make the process of selecting and installing your electronics effortless so you can focus on enjoying them. Whether you desire speakers on your terrace, a television located above your home fireplace or in your office lobby, several remote controls combined into one, or your own custom idea brought to reality, Grand Central Wiring ensures that your experience will be superior. We offer a variety of services customized to your needs.
about:
Grand Central Wiring was founded in 2006 by Jason Gillespie in Greenville, South Carolina. The company began as an audio/video design and build firm, focusing on residential and light commercial installations.

The company provides a range of services including home theater installation, TV mounting, universal remote programming, structured wiring for data, telephone, video, and security systems, as well as smart home automation, lighting control, and video surveillance. They also offer construction-related services such as design-build movie cinemas, sheetrock repair, painting, framing, and masonry through a licensed home builder, Phil Gillespie. The firm carries products from brands like Samsung, SunBriteTV, Denon, Yamaha, Sonos, and others, and wires for local TV and internet providers including Charter, AT&T, DirecTV, and Dish.

Grand Central Wiring serves homeowners, businesses, and custom home builders in the Greenville area. Projects have included outdoor terrace speakers, lobby television installations, whole-home audio distribution, and security camera systems for both new construction and retrofit applications. The company works with residential clients as well as commercial spaces such as office lobbies and gaming rooms.

The company emphasizes free estimates, a satisfaction guarantee on workmanship, and an extended warranty on products sold through them. Their stated philosophy is that technology should be easy to use and seamless, with a focus on concealing wiring and equipment while delivering reliable performance.

name: Grand Rapids Chair Company
old_description: With approachable forms, customizable finishes, and built-in power ready to go, it keeps spaces looking fresh and working smarter. Solid wood or laminate, bold base or neutral tone—Clyde plays well with others.
about:
Grand Rapids Chair Company operates from Byron Center, Michigan, where it was founded in 1991 as Manufacturer's Resource by Dave and Jill Miller. The company was renamed Grand Rapids Chair Company, and Geoff assumed leadership in 2012, growing the team to nearly 150 employees.

The company manufactures commercial-grade furniture in its West Michigan factory, working with solid hardwoods, steel, aluminum, and high-performance textiles. Its product line spans chairs, stools, benches, lounge seating, and a range of tables including communal, pedestal, occasional, and T-base models, plus outdoor collections. Finishing capabilities include over 150 powder-coat colors for metal components and a virtually unlimited selection of fabrics, all produced locally to keep lead times short and customization affordable.

Grand Rapids Chair serves the restaurant, office, hospitality, and higher-education markets, supplying design partners and specifiers who furnish gathering spaces such as cafes, hubs, and campus lounges. The portfolio emphasizes versatile, accessible products that can be tailored to specific project palettes.

A family mindset drives the business: the Millers keep manufacturing in Michigan to ensure quality control, fast delivery, and the ability to fulfill one-of-a-kind orders quickly. An warranty backs every piece, and the company maintains community ties, including a partnership with the Juvenile Diabetes Research Foundation that inspired the Brooke chair.

name: Grand Solar, Inc.
old_description: Grand Solar was established in Hawaii in 1980 and became incorporated in 1985.  During the more than 30 years of operation,  the company has consistently been a leader in design, installation and service of nearly every type of solar thermal system sold in Hawaii.  The original owner, John Grandinetti, still  is present at all of the residential and commercial solar system installations completed by the company.  In addition, the Photovoltaic systems offered by Grand Solar are US manufactured components only and  carry industry leading product warranties on performance.
about:
Grand Solar, Inc. was established in Honolulu, Hawaii, in 1980 and incorporated in 1985. The original owner, John Grandinetti, remains actively involved, attending every residential and commercial solar installation the company performs. The business began as a specialist in solar thermal system design, installation, and service, quickly becoming a leader across the Hawaiian islands.

The company designs, installs, and services a range of solar thermal technologies, including the Blazing Tubes system, conventional pump solar hot water systems, and thermosyphon solar hot water systems. It also installs residential photovoltaic systems using only U.S.-manufactured components, which carry performance warranties. Grand Solar serves both residential and commercial customers throughout Hawaii.

Grand Solar’s customer base includes homeowners and businesses seeking solar thermal and photovoltaic solutions. The company has maintained an A+ rating with the Better Business Bureau since 1990, and the Hawaii Regulated Industries Complaint Office has no record of complaints. It is also a member in good standing of the Hawaii Solar Energy Association.

Grand Solar differentiates itself through the founder’s hands-on presence at every job, a commitment to U.S.-sourced PV components, and long-standing industry affiliations that underscore its focus on reliability and customer satisfaction.

old_description: Since 1966, we’ve delivered quality custom packaging solutions. We operate as a full-service packaging partner putting exceptional customer service at the forefront of everything we do.
about:
Great American Packaging was founded in 1966 in Los Angeles, California. The company has operated continuously from its Southern California base for more than five decades, building a reputation as a full-service packaging partner.

The company manufactures custom poly bags, poly films, and specialty bags for food, ice, medical, and consumer applications. It controls the entire production process in-house, from extrusion and printing to converting finished packaging. Its facility runs state-of-the-art printing presses and extruders, enabling it to produce FDA- and USDA-approved materials that meet strict food-safety standards.

Great American Packaging serves manufacturers of health and safety products, food product suppliers, and major retail chains such as Costco and The Home Depot. Its customer base spans the food, ice, medical, and consumer-goods sectors, with a focus on flexible packaging that protects product integrity and reduces waste.

The company emphasizes a "white glove service" model that includes packaging consulting, rapid lead times, and IFS PACsecure certification for food safety. It says this end-to-end control and service commitment differentiate it from competitors that only print or convert.

It operates as a supplier and service provider, offering material selection support, project consultation, and coordination with architects and contractors. The company emphasizes honest information drawn from over 15 years of industry experience, precise orders, accurate lead times, and quality products. It positions itself as a value-driven supplier that prioritizes clear communication and reliable timelines.

about:
Great Western Products Co., LLC operates from Hollywood, Alabama. The company traces its roots back more than 50 years, starting with a focus on popcorn before expanding into a full range of concession foods. Ownership details and founder names are not publicly disclosed.

The company manufactures and supplies a wide variety of concession products including popcorn, cotton candy, snow cone syrups, floss sugars, popcorn seasonings, funnel cake and corn dog batters, and candy apple mixes. It also provides nonfood supplies such as cups, tubs, bags, and other packaging materials. Operations are split between a headquarters in Northeast Alabama and a packaging hub located in the Midwest Corn Belt, though facility size and employee count are not disclosed.

Great Western serves fair and event operators, movie theater chains, and businesses seeking private label snack brands. Its customer base includes blockbuster theater chains and international distributors across Canada, the Caribbean, Asia, Europe, and South America. The company emphasizes low minimum order quantities to accommodate businesses of all sizes.

Great Western differentiates itself through its decades of experience, a commitment to the industry's lowest minimum quantity requirements for private label programs, and a logistics footprint that keeps production close to key agricultural regions. The company also highlights strong vendor relationships and comprehensive branding support as key advantages.
